verdict.rationale: Stripe names the use case "Issuing for agents": virtual cards that agents use to buy autonomously, with spend controls and real-time authorization decisioning. Its documented spending controls block merchant categories and merchant IDs and set per-authorization or monthly limits, and cards can be scoped to a single task and invalidated after use. Coverage is still incomplete, so this is partial rather than full. missing for 10: explicit time-based card expiry configuration (only single-use invalidation is documented), explicit merchant allow-list locking (controls are documented as blocks), and independent or hands-on corroboration of the agent card flow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can give an agent its own card — issue a scoped virtual card to an AI agent with merchant locks, amount caps, and expiry so autonomous purchases stay inside policy, a use the vendor documents by name

citations.quote: Issuing for agents lets you issue virtual cards that agents can use to make purchases autonomously, with spend controls, real-time authorization decisioning, and full transaction visibility.
Issue virtual cards scoped to a single task or session. Cards are automatically invalidated after use.
You can use spending controls to block merchant categories (for example, bakeries), countries, merchant IDs, or card presence, and to set spending limits per authorization or per month.
Using the synchronous webhook, you can approve or decline authorization requests in real time.
